COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Chosen method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) implemented in an “event–study / stacked-DID” framework.

Rationale  
•  Cyclone strikes are plausibly exogenous in timing, location, and intensity once we condition on geography.  
•  We observe the same regions repeatedly before and after a land-fall episode as well as comparable regions that do **not** experience an episode during the same years.  
•  The long panel permits us to trace dynamic effects (event study) and to stack multiple events per region while avoiding contaminated post-periods (Callaway-Sant’Anna 2021; Sun & Abraham 2021).  
•  IV or RDD are less natural here: there is no clearly manipulable running variable and the main concern is *timing*, not partial compliance.  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
•  CycloneHit_{i,t} = 1 if region i experienced at least one cyclone landfall in year t with maximum sustained surface-wind speed ≥ 33 m/s (hurricane strength) within ≤ 100 km of the region centroid.  
•  Intensity_{i,t} = log(1 + Σ_{e∈E_{i,t}} WindSpeed_e × PopExposure_e) – used for intensity-weighted results.

Control group  
•  Same regions *before* they are hit (‘within-unit’) plus regions with similar baseline characteristics (latitude band, coastal distance, GDP per-capita decile, governance index) that are not hit in that calendar year.  
•  We exclude years in which *any* cyclone comes within 300 km to mitigate spillovers.

Treatment timing / event date  
•  Event year τ=0 is the first year with CycloneHit=1 after at least five cyclone-free years for that region.  
•  We stack every qualifying event; the “clock” (τ) resets and observations after τ=+T (e.g., +10) are censored to avoid overlapping post-periods.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1 Parallel Trends: In the absence of a cyclone, GDP growth in treated and control regions would have evolved similarly.  
  Plausibility: Coastal regions share similar trade exposure, climate, and infrastructure trends. We will test for pre-trends (placebo leads).

A2 No Anticipation: Economic agents cannot precisely anticipate cyclone landfalls far enough in advance to alter growth trajectories.  
  Plausibility: Exact track and intensity are only known days in advance; yearly data mitigates short-run anticipatory effects.

A3 Stable Unit Treatment Value (No Spillovers): A cyclone affecting region i does not directly change GDP in region j > 300 km away.  
  Plausibility: Physical damage is extremely local; nevertheless we will drop neighboring regions in robustness checks.

A4 Exogeneity of Treatment Intensity: Conditional on geography, the realized intensity is orthogonal to unobserved growth shocks.  
  Plausibility: Meteorological processes are unrelated to local business cycles.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1 Differential Pre-Trends  
 • Test: Event-study leads for –5 ≤ τ ≤ –1 should be jointly zero.  
 • Mitigation: Region-specific linear trends; match on pre-treatment growth.

T2 Post-Treatment Migration / Composition Changes  
 • Mitigation: Use satellite-based night-lights and remotely sensed economic activity that are population-invariant; include population as outcome to study attrition.

T3 Measurement Error in Damage / Exposure  
 • Mitigation: Cross-validate cyclone tracks with IBTrACS and ERA5 reanalysis; instrument Intensity_{i,t} with *modeled* maximum winds at land-fall (IV robustness); winsorize outliers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
###############################################################
# 0. Packages
###############################################################
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)        # fast high-dimensional fixed effects
library(did)           # Callaway-Sant’Anna stacked DID
library(modelsummary)  # nice output

###############################################################
# 1. Load and merge data
###############################################################
cyclones <- read_csv("cyclone_tracks.csv")      # one row per 6-hour point
econ     <- read_csv("region_year_gdp.csv")     # GDP pc, population, etc.
regions  <- read_csv("region_attributes.csv")   # geography controls

# Construct annual cyclone exposure for each region
cyclone_year <- cyclones %>%
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(region_id, year) %>%
  summarise(max_wind = max(wind_speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            pop_exp  = sum(population_exposed),
            hit      = as.integer(any(distance_km <= 100 & wind_speed >= 33)),
            intensity = log1p(sum(wind_speed * population_exposed))) %>%
  ungroup()

# Merge
panel <- econ %>%
  left_join(cyclone_year, by = c("region_id","year")) %>%
  left_join(regions, by = "region_id") %>%
  arrange(region_id, year) %>%
  mutate(hit = replace_na(hit, 0),
         intensity = replace_na(intensity, 0),
         gdp_growth = 100 * (log(gdp_pc) - lag(log(gdp_pc))))

###############################################################
# 2. Event-study / stacked DID preparation
###############################################################
# Identify first hit after ≥5 calm years
panel <- panel %>%
  group_by(region_id) %>%
  mutate(last_hit = lag(cumsum(hit)>0),
         calm_yrs = cumsum(!hit) - cummax((cumsum(!hit))*hit),
         first_hit = hit == 1 & calm_yrs >= 5) %>%
  ungroup()

# Event time
panel <- panel %>%
  group_by(region_id) %>%
  mutate(event_time = if_else(cumsum(first_hit)>0,
                              year - first(year[first_hit==1]), NA_integer_)) %>%
  ungroup()

###############################################################
# 3. Main specification: two-way FE DID
###############################################################
est_main <- feols(gdp_growth ~ hit | region_id + year,
                  data = panel,
                  cluster = ~region_id)
summary(est_main)

###############################################################
# 4. Event-study (lead/lag dummies)
###############################################################
# Build bins: −5 to +10, omit −1 as reference
for (k in -5:10) {
  panel[[paste0("tau",k)]] <- as.integer(panel$event_time == k)
}
panel$tau_m1 <- NULL  # drop reference category

leadlag_vars <- names(panel)[grep("^tau", names(panel))]

formula_es <- reformulate(leadlag_vars,
                          response = "gdp_growth")

est_es <- feols(formula_es | region_id + year,
                data = panel,
                cluster = ~region_id)
iplot(est_es, ci_level = 0.90, ref.line = 0)

###############################################################
# 5. Robustness: drop neighboring regions
###############################################################
panel_rb <- panel %>% filter(min_distance_to_hit > 300 | is.na(min_distance_to_hit))
est_rb <- feols(gdp_growth ~ hit | region_id + year,
                data = panel_rb,
                cluster = ~region_id)
etable(est_main, est_rb, dict = c(hit = "Cyclone Hit"))
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Prior sign: Negative.  
Magnitude: A baseline guess from the disaster-economics literature is a 1.0–1.5 ppt reduction in real GDP per-capita growth in the first year, with partial rebound but a remaining level loss of ~3–5 % after a decade for a category-3 (≥ 50 m/s) land-fall.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1 Parallel pre-trends checked and satisfied: 1  
C2 No anticipation: 0.8 (near-term behavioral changes possible)  
C3 No spillovers/ interference: 0.7  
C4 No time-varying confounders coincident with treatment: 0.7  
C5 Treatment not manipulable by units: 1  

Total (out of 5) = 4.2  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
End of research plan
